Nel mieloma multiplo la TC «total body»:
In multiple myeloma, low-dose "whole-body" CT has replaced the old skeletal survey (IMWG guidelines): a single lytic lesion of at least 5 mm is enough to define the bone disease requiring therapy (CRAB criterion, "B" = bone). Lesions are lytic, without a sclerotic rim; in this patient the vertebral bodies from T9 to L1 have cancellous bone replaced by tissue of 20-45 HU (T8 is heterogeneous, with lytic areas and denser areas), whereas in healthy vertebrae cancellous bone measures 130-290 HU.

Dual-energy CT makes it possible to "remove" calcium (virtual non-calcium): in adults normal bone marrow is largely fat and appears dark (negative values), whereas marrow infiltrated by plasma cells is bright, as on T1 MRI. It is also useful where the cortex is not yet eroded: here the affected vertebrae measure about 5-20 HU, the healthy ones from -40 to -130 HU.

Things to report: levels involved, largest lesions, integrity of the posterior wall and canal, fracture risk (SINS), extraosseous masses. Lesions should be counted starting from the sacrum or from C2 (use the sagittal MPR reconstructions).

Pitfalls: do not confuse diffuse osteoporosis (reduced density but preserved fat) with infiltration; in a treated patient, lesions may become sclerotic during response (T8 here has denser areas).
Nel mieloma cerca lesioni litiche ≥ 5 mm: In myeloma look for lytic lesions ≥ 5 mm throughout the spine; with dual energy, bright marrow on the calcium-free map means infiltration.
